prompt:
以下は、あるVoices/Perspective型記事(3 Voices版)の5つのsection本文
(Voice 1〜3/Tension/Closing)です。それぞれについて、指定された項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

【Voice 1〜3に共通で適用する7項目(2026-09-17ユーザー正式決定で候補C/leak_position_blur追加)】
- leak_evidence_subject: 文の主語がsurvey/research/data/percentageになっている文が無い場合PASS
- leak_numbers_foreground: 具体的な数字が、その人物自身の経験に属する数値であり、かつその人の
  経験の描写より前面に出ていない場合PASS(数字が0個、またはその人物自身の経験に属する数字が
  1個だけ実感として自然に織り込まれている場合はPASS。survey/report/study等、本人の経験に
  属さない外部統計をVoice内で論証材料として使っている場合はFAIL)
- leak_narrator_analysis: Narrator(語り手)が、Voiceの人物を外側から分析・要約していない場合PASS
- leak_unknowable_analysis: その人物自身が実際に考え・言いそうにない、外部の分析的視点を、その人の
  Perspectiveとして書いていない場合PASS
- leak_discovery_syntax: Discovery/Trend記事のような文構造へ戻っていない場合PASS
- leak_evidence_memorable: Evidenceよりもその人物の経験・感情の方が記憶に残る書き方になっている場合PASS
- leak_position_blur: このVoiceが、自分の立場の中の迷い・葛藤(nuance)の範囲を超えて、他の
  Voice(相手側)が中心的に抱えている懸念・反論そのものを、自分の中心的な主張として代弁して
  いない場合PASS(相手側の中心論点をこのVoiceが実質的に引き受けてしまっている場合はFAIL)

いずれのVoiceについても、他のVoiceと同一の基準で判定してください(特定の立場が抽象的な
代弁者の解説になっている場合は、leak_evidence_subject/leak_narrator_analysis/leak_discovery_syntax
のいずれかでFAILとしてください)。

【Tensionに適用する項目】
- leak_evidence_subject / leak_discovery_syntax / leak_evidence_memorable: 上記と同じ意味
  (Tension本文に対して判定)
- leak_numbers_foreground(Tension用): 具体的な数字・比較結果が、3人の合理性を制約する力の
  描写より前面に出ていない場合PASS(Tensionは1人の経験ではなく複数人の力関係を扱うため、
  Voice用の「本人の経験に属する数値」限定はここでは適用しない)
- leak_tension_reverts_to_research: Tensionの中心が、3人がなぜ違う答えに至るのかの掘り下げになって
  おり、survey/研究データそのものの説明・比較へ戻っていない場合PASS
- leak_binary_camp_split: Tensionが3人を単純に対称的な2対1の陣営へ分けて描いていない場合PASS
  (分けている場合FAIL)

【Closingに適用する1項目】
- leak_closing_simple_summary: Closingが、単なる要約や「人による」という結び方だけで終わっておらず、
  かつWriter自身の解決策・妥協案の提案になっていない場合PASS

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください。FAILの場合はquoted_evidenceに該当する
原文を引用してください(英語本文をそのまま引用してよい)。PASSの場合quoted_evidenceは空文字列に
してください。

【Voice 1本文】
I want my work and experience to decide whether I get an interview. I do not want a hidden score to decide my future before a person hears from me.

When an AI system reads my application, I may not know which words it wants. In a video interview, it may study my voice, face, or speaking style. But I may not know if those signs truly show how well I can do the job.

This fear is not only an idea. One applicant in Massachusetts said that a hiring system gave him scores for qualities such as trust and honesty. He said he could not refuse the AI interview. He also could not challenge the result. He was not hired.

That leaves me with no clear path. If I am rejected, I need to know what happened. I need a way to ask for a human review. Without that, I may feel that I was judged by a rule I could not see and could not question.

I understand that companies receive many applications. I also understand that people make mistakes. But if AI controls my chance to enter the process, I need a fair way to understand and question its decision.

【Voice 2本文】
I use AI because hiring work can become too large for a small team. It can sort applications, plan interviews, and help write job posts. This gives me more time to speak with candidates and managers.

But I cannot simply say, “The computer chose you” or “The computer rejected you.” Candidates want to know if the process is fair. Many already believe that AI screening can be biased.

So I need more than a tool. I need records of how it works. I need clear information about what the system measures. I also need regular bias checks. If the results are different for different groups of people, I must see that problem and act on it.

I must prepare simple information for candidates. I should be able to tell them where AI is used and what happens next. If a candidate raises a concern, I need a real answer, not a general promise that the system is fair.

This creates pressure in my daily work. AI may save time, but I remain responsible for the hiring process. If I cannot explain a score, I cannot confidently use it. If I cannot show that the process is fair, the tool becomes a risk instead of help.

【Voice 3本文】
I look at every hiring cost. Open jobs can slow down the business. A long hiring process can make good candidates leave. AI may cut the time needed to find people from weeks to only a few days. It may also reduce hiring costs.

Those gains matter to me. They can help the company serve customers and keep operating. If I do not control costs, I may not be able to protect the jobs of the people already here.

But speed is not the only cost. If an AI system treats people unfairly, the company may face a legal claim. We may have to pay damages. We may also lose the trust of candidates, workers, and customers. A damaged name can stay with the company for years.

I therefore need to know more than whether the tool is fast. I need to know what it does when it makes a mistake. I need clear records, human checks, and a plan for complaints. These controls may slow hiring and cost money. Yet using the system without them could cost much more.

My decision is not simply “use AI” or “do not use AI.” I must decide whether the savings are worth the risks for this company, this job, and these candidates.

【Tension本文】
These three needs do not fit together easily. The applicant wants a clear reason and a chance to challenge the result. That review takes time. The recruiter wants enough control and evidence to explain the process. Audits and records take staff and money. The owner wants the hiring process to stay fast and affordable. Extra steps can reduce the savings that made AI attractive.

A system can also look efficient from the owner’s desk while feeling unfair to the applicant. A recruiter may have a fairness document but still be unable to explain one person’s rejection. A human review may help one applicant, but it may also make the process slower for thousands of others.

The difficult question is therefore not only whether AI can find candidates quickly. It is whether the company can use it while giving each rejected person a meaningful explanation and a real way to raise a concern. The owner must pay for that protection. The recruiter must carry it out. The applicant must live with the result.

【Closing本文】
AI can make hiring faster, but it cannot remove responsibility from the people who use it. An applicant still needs a fair chance. A recruiter still needs to prove that the process is fair. An owner still needs to protect the company from legal and financial harm.

For now, every company using AI faces this choice in practical terms: save time today, or spend more time checking the system before harm grows. The answer will shape not only how quickly a person is hired, but also whether that person can understand why the door opened—or why it closed.

voice_1.reasoning: 全体は応募者の一人称の不安と必要を中心にしているが、途中で語り手が外部事例を持ち込み、「この恐れは単なる考えではない」と証拠化している。これにより、当事者の経験ではなく記事側の立証・発見の構文が一部混入している。
voice_1.quoted_evidence: “This fear is not only an idea. One applicant in Massachusetts said that a hiring system gave him scores for qualities such as trust and honesty.”

voice_2.reasoning: 採用担当者の一人称で、効率化の利点と、説明責任・監査・候補者対応を負う立場が具体的に描かれている。候補者の懸念に触れてはいるが、それを採用担当者自身の責任と日常的な判断の問題として扱っており、立場の中心がぼやけていない。

voice_3.reasoning: 会社所有者のコスト、事業継続、法的リスク、信頼維持という判断軸は一貫している。一方、冒頭でAIの効果を「数週間から数日」という比較で前面に提示しており、本人の具体的経験というより一般的な効率性の主張が先行している。
voice_3.quoted_evidence: “AI may cut the time needed to find people from weeks to only a few days. It may also reduce hiring costs.”

tension.reasoning: 研究結果や統計の比較ではなく、説明・監査・人間による再審査が、時間・費用・大量処理能力と衝突する仕組みを3人の立場から掘り下げている。3人を単純な賛成派と反対派に分けず、それぞれが異なる制約を抱えている形になっている。

closing.reasoning: 3人の要点を再確認しつつ、AI導入後も責任が残ることと、説明可能性が採用結果への信頼を左右することを示している。Writer独自の解決策や妥協案を提示するだけの結び、または「人による」という単純な要約にはなっていない。
